paired_controls.method: Separate persistent Python processes retain their own calibrated integrators and default allocator heaps. Only one process integrates at a time. Eight adjacent AB/BA pairs per comparison, Poisson errors, 56 references to warmed inputs, >=one batch per block targeting 0.5 s. No setup in timed comparisons and no allocator override. This controls elapsed-session drift better than distant fresh-process medians; simultaneous resident calibration tables may affect cache conditions. Both sides must meet the 3.6 other-busy-core screen for a pair to qualify.

release.protocol: Python batch1d on 56 references to preloaded float64 images, 2000 uniform 2theta bins, masks, polarization 0.965 and solid-angle correction. Supersampling n=15 for Pilatus1M and n=5 for Eiger9M; pixel_split has no n. One global Rayon pool configured to 1/2/4/8; three warmed blocks per error mode targeting 0.5 s; two fresh process trials. Imports, pool configuration and input preloading excluded from setup; cold geometry, LUT creation, denominator preparation and first Poisson result included. RSS sampled externally every 10 ms. All final points satisfy median other CPU load <=3.6 logical cores in both error modes; failed attempts retained. Paired AB/BA comparisons at 1 and 8 workers run only one integrator process at a time. Official licensed 0.5.5 and CI-built licensed 0.6.0 wheels, with fast_math argument omitted. No allocator override or machine-specific compiler flags. SFSCXRD temporarily paused under authorization and resumed; Peritheos validation allowed to finish. Additional Dioptas/PhaseSmith calculations temporarily paused and resumed under separate explicit authorization.

paired_controls.protocol: Four adjacent AB/BA pairs at eight workers, Poisson errors, 56 warmed frame references, targeting 0.5 seconds per block. Separate persistent processes, only one integrating at a time. Both sides must satisfy <=3.6 other busy logical cores. Resident calibration data in the idle process can change cache conditions; use this as a control alongside fresh-process results.

comparison.protocol: Same preloaded float64 images, masks, geometry, 2000 2theta bins, polarization 0.965, solid-angle correction, 56 frame references, Poisson on/off, 1/2/4/8 Python frame threads, two fresh-process trials, three warmed timing blocks targeting 0.5 s, 10 ms external RSS sampling and <=3.6-other-busy-core median screen in both error modes. Imports and input warm-up excluded. pyFAI uses a shallow geometry copy and a separate initialized CSR engine per worker, initialized sequentially from shared geometry arrays; first-result and all-workers-ready setup times are both recorded. pyFAI uses safe=True and its native float32 CSR data path. The installed macOS wheel has no libomp dependency; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 prevents nested parallelism. azint shares the sparse matrix through shallow copies, uses n=15/5, and integrates on Python frame threads; OMP_NUM_THREADS equals c only for its parallel matrix construction. azint generic and CPU/LTO/fast-math builds are separate variants. No claims of identical algorithms or output patterns between libraries.
